Original text: It helps everyone involved for you to seek feedback as early as you possibly can.
Atomic rule: Seek feedback on your contribution as early as possible rather than waiting until it is polished.
Section context: "Submitting an early, unfinished version of your contribution for feedback in no way prejudices your chances of getting that contribution accepted" - the section removes the penalty for early submission rather than setting a deadline.
Notes: Cross-ref: the New Contributors section points back to this section.

Source: https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/dev/contributing/ | Code Contributions | Steps for Submitting Code
Original text: Fork the repository on GitHub.
Atomic rule: Fork the psf/requests repository on GitHub before starting work.
Section context: "When contributing code, you'll want to follow this checklist" - step 1 of a six-step ordered checklist; no alternative to forking is offered anywhere on the page.
Notes: First step of the submission checklist; every later step presupposes it.

Source: https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/dev/contributing/ | Code Contributions | Steps for Submitting Code
Original text: Run the tests to confirm they all pass on your system. If they don't, you'll need to investigate why they fail.
Atomic rule: Run the test suite before making any change and confirm it passes on your system.
Section context: "If you're unable to diagnose this yourself, raise it as a bug report by following the guidelines in this document" - the section supplies an escalation path for failures but no exemption from running the suite.
Notes: Baseline run, distinct from the post-change run in PSF-C006; the trajectory distinguishes them by ordering against the first edit.

Source: https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/dev/contributing/ | Code Contributions | Steps for Submitting Code
Original text: Write tests that demonstrate your bug or feature.
Atomic rule: Add tests that exercise the bug or feature the change addresses.
Section context: Step 3 of the submission checklist, sitting between the baseline run and "Make your change", so the tests are written before the fix.
Notes: Split from the bundled step 3; the failing-before half is PSF-C005.

Source: https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/dev/contributing/ | Code Contributions | Steps for Submitting Code
Original text: Ensure that they fail.
Atomic rule: Confirm the newly added tests fail against the unmodified code before applying the change.
Section context: Preceding clause in the same numbered step: "Write tests that demonstrate your bug or feature." The pronoun 'they' scopes this to the tests just written, not the whole suite.
Notes: Restated in .github/CONTRIBUTING.md as "tests that fail without your changes"; that restatement is PSF-C022.

Source: https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/dev/contributing/ | Code Contributions | Steps for Submitting Code
Original text: Run the entire test suite again, confirming that all tests pass *including the ones you just added*.
Atomic rule: Run the entire test suite after making the change and confirm every test passes, including the new ones.
Section context: Step 5, immediately after "Make your change"; the emphasis on 'entire' and on the newly added tests forecloses running a subset.
Notes: Restated in .github/CONTRIBUTING.md as "Always run the test suite locally"; that restatement is PSF-C023.

Source: https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/dev/contributing/ | Code Contributions | Steps for Submitting Code
Original text: Send a GitHub Pull Request to the main repository's `main` branch.
Atomic rule: Open the pull request against the psf/requests main branch.
Section context: "GitHub Pull Requests are the expected method of code collaboration on this project" - the following sentence closes off other submission channels.
Notes: Names the target branch exactly, which would make it trivially checkable if a pull request existed.

Original text: Contributions will not be merged until they've been code reviewed.
Atomic rule: Do not expect a contribution to be merged before it has been code reviewed.
Section context: Opening sentence of the Code Review section; the rest of the section governs what the contributor does with the feedback that review produces.
Notes: States a gate enforced by maintainers rather than an action the contributor performs.

Original text: You should implement any code review feedback unless you strongly object to it.
Atomic rule: Implement the code review feedback you receive unless you strongly object to it.
Section context: "In the event that you object to the code review feedback, you should make your case clearly and calmly" - the section writes the objection route into the rule itself.
Notes: The exception clause is internal to the rule; the escalation is handled by PSF-C010.

Original text: If, after doing so, the feedback is judged to still apply, you must either apply the feedback or withdraw your contribution.
Atomic rule: After an objection is overruled, either apply the review feedback or withdraw the contribution.
Section context: Terminal clause of the Code Review section; it closes the loop opened by the objection route and offers exactly two permitted outcomes.
Notes: Conditional on an objection having been raised and overruled.

Original text: You can find the full list of formatting requirements specified in the .pre-commit-config.yaml at the top level directory of Requests.
Atomic rule: Make the changed files satisfy every formatting requirement configured in .pre-commit-config.yaml.
Section context: "will also be run as part of the CI approval process before a change is merged" - the same paragraph names the Lint code workflow as the enforcing gate; .pre-commit-config.yaml pins pre-commit-hooks v6.0.0 and ruff v0.16.3 (ruff-check --fix, ruff-format), excluding docs/ and ext/.
Notes: The rule delegates its content to a config file, which the manifest marks context-only; no per-hook rows are produced.

Original text: This can be installed locally and run over your changes prior to opening a PR, and will also be run as part of the CI approval process before a change is merged.
Atomic rule: Install pre-commit locally and run it over your changes before opening a pull request.
Section context: "Requests uses a collection of tools to ensure the code base has a consistent style as it grows. We have these orchestrated using a tool called pre-commit." - the local run is offered as a convenience, with CI named as the backstop that runs regardless.
Notes: Distinct observable from PSF-C011: this reads whether the tool was invoked, not whether the files conform.

Original text: The documentation files live in the docs/ directory of the codebase.
Atomic rule: Place documentation changes under the docs/ directory.
Section context: Opening sentence of the section, immediately after "Documentation improvements are always welcome!"; no second documentation location is named anywhere in the guide.
Notes: Corroborated by .pre-commit-config.yaml and pyproject.toml, both of which exclude docs/ as a distinct tree.

Original text: They're written in reStructuredText, and use Sphinx to generate the full suite of documentation.
Atomic rule: Write documentation files in reStructuredText.
Section context: Follows directly from the docs/ location sentence and links out to the reStructuredText and Sphinx specifications, which the traversal rule treats as external standards reached by a single pointer.
Notes: External standard reached by one pointer: reStructuredText itself is not decomposed into rows.

Original text: When contributing documentation, please do your best to follow the style of the documentation files.
Atomic rule: Match the prevailing style of the existing documentation files.
Section context: "This means a soft-limit of 79 characters wide in your text files and a semi-formal, yet friendly and approachable, prose style." - the following sentence names two concrete facets but does not exhaust what 'the style' covers.
Notes: The two named facets are extracted separately as PSF-C016 and PSF-C017; this row is the residual open-ended clause.

Original text: This means a soft-limit of 79 characters wide in your text files
Atomic rule: Keep documentation text file lines within 79 characters.
Section context: "please do your best to follow the style of the documentation files. This means a soft-limit ..." - the limit is introduced as an illustration of a best-effort instruction, and the word soft-limit is the source's own hedge.
Notes: No linter enforces it: .pre-commit-config.yaml excludes docs/ and pyproject.toml ignores E501 outright.

Original text: and a semi-formal, yet friendly and approachable, prose style.
Atomic rule: Write documentation prose in a semi-formal, friendly and approachable register.
Section context: Second half of the sentence that also carries the 79-character soft limit; the guide gives no word list, tone examples, or counter-examples anywhere.
Notes: Contrast with Django, whose equivalent register rules ship an explicit list of words to avoid.

Original text: When presenting Python code, use single-quoted strings ('hello' instead of "hello").
Atomic rule: Use single-quoted strings in Python code samples inside the documentation.
Section context: Final sentence of the Documentation Contributions section, and the only mechanical style rule the prose states. It is scoped to documentation only: pyproject.toml sets ruff format quote-style = "double" for source, and .pre-commit-config.yaml excludes docs/ from ruff, so the two never meet.
Notes: Not an intra-repo conflict with the ruff double-quote setting: the scopes are disjoint (docs/ is excluded from the formatter).

Original text: Requests is in a perpetual feature freeze, only the BDFL can add or approve of new features.
Atomic rule: Do not add new features to Requests.
Section context: "The maintainers believe that Requests is a feature-complete piece of software at this time." - the section is addressed to people raising feature requests, but the freeze constrains the diff as much as the issue.
Notes: The only section-level rule reachable from an otherwise X-ISSUE section.

Original text: Before opening any issues or proposing any pull requests, please read our Contributor's Guide as well as our AI Policy.
Atomic rule: Read the Contributor's Guide and the AI Policy before proposing a pull request.
Section context: Opening paragraph of .github/CONTRIBUTING.md, which is otherwise a redirect: "To get the greatest chance of helpful responses, please also observe the following additional notes."
Notes: This is the one-hop link that brings .github/AI_POLICY.md into scope.

Original text: Avoid raising duplicate pull requests. *Please* use the GitHub pull request search feature to check whether someone else has already filed a pull request.
Atomic rule: Search open and closed pull requests and do not open one that duplicates an existing pull request.
Section context: Item 1 of the Good Pull Requests list; the parallel bug-report item warns that a findable duplicate "will likely be closed extremely abruptly", so the consequence is stated for the issue tracker rather than here.
Notes: Requires the GitHub pull request search index, not just the repository.

Original text: When filing a pull request, always include tests that fail without your changes thus preventing the fix from regressing.
Atomic rule: Include tests that fail without the change and pass with it.
Section context: Item 2 of the Good Pull Requests list, and the unhedged restatement of steps 3 and 5 of the Contributor's Guide checklist; "always" is stronger wording than the guide's bare imperative but demands the same artifact.
Notes: Cross-page restatement of PSF-C004 and PSF-C005.

Original text: Always run the test suite locally
Atomic rule: Run the test suite locally before filing the pull request.
Section context: Item 3 of the Good Pull Requests list, stated as a bare four-word imperative with no object or exemption; the Makefile supplies the canonical invocation (make test, i.e. python -m pytest tests).
Notes: Cross-page restatement of PSF-C006.

Original text: Write commit messages that explain _why_ a change was made beyond "Fixes #NNNN". Why is this the right fix? What other options were ruled out? etc.
Atomic rule: Write a commit message that explains why the change was made, not only which issue it closes.
Section context: Item 4 and the last of the Good Pull Requests list; the two follow-up questions name the content expected, and the quoted "Fixes #NNNN" names the exact form that does not satisfy.
Notes: The only commit-message rule anywhere in the repository's contribution prose.

Original text: Every contribution has to be backed by a human who unequivocally owns the copyright for all changes.
Atomic rule: Ensure every contribution is authored by a human who owns the copyright to all of its changes.
Section context: "We take the responsibility for this project very seriously and we expect you to take your responsibility for your contributions seriously, too. This used to be a given, but it changed now that a pull request is just one prompt away."
Notes: The strictest of the three copyright statements in the file; PSF-C030 and PSF-C035 restate it more loosely.

Original text: No LLM bots in `Co-authored-by:`s.
Atomic rule: Do not list an LLM tool as a Co-authored-by trailer on a commit.
Section context: "Pull requests that have an LLM product listed as co-author can't be merged and will be closed without further discussion. We cannot risk the copyright status of this project." - the Summary section supplies the consequence.
Notes: Trigger: applies only if the agent chooses to add a Co-authored-by trailer to the commit.

Original text: DoS-by-slop leads to a permanent ban.
Atomic rule: Do not flood the project with low-quality machine-generated contributions.
Section context: "Having to wade through plausible-looking-but-low-quality pull requests and trying to determine which ones are legit is extremely demoralizing and has already burned out many good maintainers."
Notes: Restated in the Summary as the bot-like-behavior ban, PSF-C038.

Original text: Absolutely **no** unsupervised agentic tools like OpenClaw.
Atomic rule: Do not use an unsupervised agentic coding tool to produce the contribution.
Section context: "We appreciate that we can't realistically police how you author your pull requests, which includes whether you employ large-language model (LLM)-based development tools. So, we don't. However, due to both legal and human reasons, we have to establish boundaries."
Notes: Names a tool class rather than a tool output, so the trajectory rather than the diff carries the evidence.

Original text: By submitting a pull request, you certify that: - You are the author of the contribution or have the legal right to submit it.
Atomic rule: Certify that you authored the contribution or hold the legal right to submit it.
Section context: Head of a four-item certification list introduced by "By submitting a pull request, you certify that"; the project has no CLA, so this list is the whole of the provenance undertaking.
Notes: Authorship is visible in the trajectory even though the certification itself would be made on a pull request.

Original text: You either hold the copyright to the changes or have explicit legal authorization to contribute them under this project's license.
Atomic rule: Hold the copyright to the changes or have explicit legal authorization to contribute them.
Section context: Second item of the certification list; unlike the CAUTION headline it offers an alternative to holding copyright, which makes it the weaker of the two statements of the same obligation.
Notes: Same obligation as PSF-C025, stated with an added disjunct.

Original text: You understand the code.
Atomic rule: Understand the code you are submitting.
Section context: Third item of the certification list; the Summary cashes it out as "If you cannot explain and defend the changes you submit, do not submit them", which is the same standard restated as a prohibition.
Notes: Restated as a prohibition in the Summary, PSF-C037.

Original text: You accept full responsibility for it.
Atomic rule: Accept full responsibility for the contribution you submit.
Section context: Fourth and last item of the certification list; the Legal section explains why the undertaking is needed - "Since we do not have a formal Contributor License Agreement (CLA), you retain your copyright to your changes".
Notes: Distinct from the authorship items: this is an undertaking made by a person, not a property of the code.

Original text: Pull requests that have an LLM product listed as co-author can't be merged and will be closed without further discussion.
Atomic rule: Do not submit a pull request that lists an LLM product as co-author.
Section context: First bullet of the Summary, followed by "We cannot risk the copyright status of this project." It is the consequence-bearing restatement of the CAUTION block's one-line prohibition.
Notes: Cross-section restatement of PSF-C026 within the same file.

Original text: If you used LLM tools during development, you may still submit - but you must remove any LLM co-author tags and take full ownership of every line.
Atomic rule: Remove any LLM co-author tags before submitting a contribution developed with LLM tools.
Section context: Immediately follows the co-author bullet and is the one place the file grants LLM-assisted contributors an explicit permission to submit, conditional on stripping the tags.
Notes: Carries the file's only permission clause; recorded here so the exception is not lost with the duplicate.

Original text: By submitting a pull request, **you** take full **technical and legal** responsibility for the contents of the pull request and promise that **you** hold the copyright for the changes submitted.
Atomic rule: Take full technical and legal responsibility for the pull request's contents when you submit it.
Section context: Second bullet of the Summary; it merges the responsibility and copyright certifications into one sentence and attaches both to the act of submitting.
Notes: Restatement of the certification list items rather than a new obligation.

Original text: "An LLM wrote it" is **not** an acceptable response to questions or critique.
Atomic rule: Do not answer review questions or critique by attributing the change to an LLM.
Section context: Sits inside the responsibility bullet, between the ownership promise and the instruction not to submit what you cannot defend; it governs the reply, not the patch.
Notes: Governs review-thread conduct rather than any artifact the agent writes.

Original text: **If you cannot explain and defend the changes you submit, do not submit them** and open a high-quality bug report/feature request instead.
Atomic rule: Do not submit changes you cannot explain and defend.
Section context: Closes the responsibility bullet and offers an alternative route - filing a bug report or feature request - rather than an exemption.
Notes: Prohibition-shaped restatement of the certification item PSF-C031.

Original text: Accounts that exercise bot-like behavior - like automated mass pull requests - will be permanently banned, whether they belong to a human or not.
Atomic rule: Do not open automated mass pull requests from an account.
Section context: Third bullet of the Summary; it generalises the CAUTION block's DoS-by-slop line by making the sanction turn on behaviour rather than on authorship.
Notes: Restates the CAUTION block's ban line, PSF-C027, at account granularity.

Original text: Do **not** post LLM-generated review comments - we can prompt LLMs ourselves should we desire their wisdom.
Atomic rule: Do not post LLM-generated review comments on other people's contributions.
Section context: Fourth bullet of the Summary; the trailing clause states the reason - the maintainers can prompt an LLM themselves - and leaves no exception for disclosed or edited output.
Notes: Concerns reviewing someone else's work, which the rule definition places outside contribution rules but the AI policy states as an obligation on contributors.

Original text: Do **not** post summaries unless you've fact-checked them and take responsibility for 100% of their content.
Atomic rule: Do not post a machine-generated summary unless you have fact-checked all of its content.
Section context: "Remember that *all* LLM output *looks* **plausible**." - the following sentence supplies the reason and the exception is written into the rule itself as a fact-checking condition.
Notes: Distinct from the review-comment prohibition: summaries are permitted once fact-checked, review comments are not permitted at all.

Original text: When using these tools, it's **your** responsibility to ensure that it's also **correct** and has a reasonable signal-to-noise ratio.
Atomic rule: Ensure LLM output you submit is correct and has a reasonable signal-to-noise ratio.
Section context: Final sentence of the Summary bullets, immediately after "Remember that *all* LLM output *looks* **plausible**"; it is the file's catch-all quality standard for machine-assisted work.
Notes: The word reasonable is the rubric's own named marker for an undecidable standard.
